title: Predicting ORT Examination Scores from Sequential Mock Examinations: An Ensemble Regression Study on Kyrgyz Secondary School Data
content: The Kyrgyz national university entrance examination (ORT) is the primary gateway to higher education in Kyrgyzstan, yet no data-driven tool exists to predict final ORT performance from sequential preparatory mock examinations. We address this gap using a labelled dataset of 374 secondary school students who sat five TSOOMO mock exams and a subsequent real ORT. The prediction target is the continuous ORT score (range 0-245). We engineer 24 features encoding the mean, last, trend, and standard deviation of subject scores across mocks, augmented by a weighted composite (calc_mean) that mirrors the official weighting formula. A systematic comparison of nine model families shows that Random Forest achieves the lowest test-set mean absolute error (MAE = 8.09, 95% CI [6.65, 9.58]; RMSE = 11.34; R2=0.884), reducing error by 71% relative to a naive mean-prediction baseline (MAE = 27.67). Five-fold cross-validation confirms stability (R2=0.912 ± 0.019). An ablation study demonstrates that removing calc_mean increases MAE by 1.42 points (+18%), confirming its importance while ruling out feature leakage. SHAP attribution reveals dominant interaction between calc_mean and analogy_mean. Fairness evaluation across gender, language, and region subgroups shows consistent performance with no systematic bias. A parallel OLS analysis with forward AIC stepwise selection retains only two features, yielding R2=0.875 with well-behaved residuals. A pseudo-labelling experiment with 160 additional unlabelled students yields negligible gain, and hyperparameter optimisation does not improve upon default Random Forest settings.
